title: [Issue]: Collections missing artwork
body:
### Please describe your bug

I started uploading my media in the previous days so I don't know if this is a recent problem, but a bug number of automatically created collections by TMDb Box Sets Plugin don't get any artwork downloaded. Even if I click on Edit Images and then Search, no singe image is feched. 

I created a [post](https://<redacted-host>/t-collections-don-t-have-thumbnails) in the forum, so apparently I'm not the only one with this problem.

### Jellyfin Version

10.8.z

### if other:

10.8.11

### Environment

```markdown
- OS: Unraid
```


### Jellyfin logs

```shell
This is the log when clicking on Refresh metadata:

[2023-11-04 21:10:26.110 +01:00] [INF] [76] Jellyfin.Plugin.KodiSyncQueue.EntryPoints.LibrarySyncNotification: Started library sync
[2023-11-04 21:10:26.168 +01:00] [INF] [76] Jellyfin.Plugin.KodiSyncQueue.EntryPoints.LibrarySyncNotification: Library Sync: Updated 1 items
[2023-11-04 21:10:26.168 +01:00] [INF] [76] Jellyfin.Plugin.KodiSyncQueue.EntryPoints.LibrarySyncNotification: Finished library sync, taking "00:00:00.0581887"
```


### FFmpeg logs

_No response_

### Please attach any browser or client logs here

_No response_

### Please attach any screenshots here

![Screenshot from 2023-11-04 21-12-29](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/assets/49582442/dffd24ad-bea0-4fdd-9829-eda972f8cf32)

comments.body:
Following our amazing friend here, I've rewritten it in bash so those of us that are running docker can also use this workaround without having to install any new dependencies on our Docker containers.

> As a workaround, launch this script for a Linux Jellyfin server with php CLI, no dependency required : (#php collection.php) [collection.txt](https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin/files/13325363/collection.txt)
> 
> ```
> <?php
>  if(php_sapi_name() != "cli")
>   exit("This script is intended to be run from the CLI");
> 
>  $TMDBAPIKEY = "4219e299c89411838049ab0dab19ebd5";
>  $DIR = "/var/lib/jellyfin/data/collections";
> 
>  $TMDBURL = "https://<redacted-host>/3/collection";
>  $IMAGEURL = "https://<redacted-host>/t/p/original";
> 
>  foreach(scandir($DIR) as $entry) {
>   if($entry == "." || $entry == "..")
>    continue;
> 
>   $xmlpath = "$DIR/$entry/collection.xml";
> 
>   if(!file_exists($xmlpath)) {
>    echo "File not found: \"$xmlpath\"\n";
>    continue;
>   }
> 
>   $posterpath = "$DIR/$entry/folder.jpg";
>   $backdroppath = "$DIR/$entry/background.jpg";
>   $posterexist = file_exists($posterpath);
>   $backdropexist = file_exists($backdroppath);
> 
>   if($posterexist && $backdropexist)
>    continue;
> 
>   $xml = file_get_contents($xmlpath);
>   $collection = new SimpleXMLElement($xml);
>   $tmdb = $collection->TmdbId;
> 
>   if(!$tmdb) {
>    echo "No TMDb ID in: \"$xmlpath\"\n";
>    continue;
>   }
> 
>   $url = "$TMDBURL/$tmdb?api_key=$TMDBAPIKEY&append_to_response=images&include_image_language=fr,null,en&language=fr-FR";
>   $json = @file_get_contents($url);
> 
>   if(!$json) {
>    echo "Failed to retrieve TMDb data: \"$url\"\n";
>    continue;
>   }
> 
>   $obj = json_decode($json, true);
> 
>   if(!$posterexist) {
>    $poster = $obj["poster_path"];
> 
>    if($poster) {
>     $posterurl = "$IMAGEURL$poster";
> 
>     echo "Downloading poster: \"$posterurl\"\n";
>     $image = file_get_contents($posterurl);
>     echo "Writing poster: \"$posterpath\"\n";
>     file_put_contents($posterpath, $image);
>    } else
>     echo "No poster: \"$DIR/$entry\"\n";
>   }
> 
>   if(!$backdropexist) {
>    $backdrop = $obj["backdrop_path"];
> 
>    if($backdrop) {
>     $backdropurl = "$IMAGEURL$backdrop";
> 
>     echo "Downloading backdrop: \"$backdropurl\"\n";
>     $image = file_get_contents($backdropurl);
>     echo "Writing backdrop: \"$backdroppath\"\n";
>     file_put_contents($backdroppath, $image);
>    } else
>     echo "No backdrop: \"$DIR/$entry\"\n";
>   }
>  }
> ?>
> ```
> 
> It browse all "/var/lib/jellyfin/data/collections" directory, and look inside all XML file for TMDb ID, it download all missing folder.jpg (poster) and background.jpg (backdrop) from TMDb API in best quality. It use the Jellyfin API Key but you can change it.
> 
> You can also delete all subdir inside "/var/lib/jellyfin/data/collections" and launch BOXSet refresh in jellyfin admin board + launch this script to get the best last and sync collection folder.
> 
> If you launch another time you get usefull information about missing picture for some movie collection or some dead collection TMDb ID in your database.
> 
> ![Sans titre](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4873680/282223489-22f110c7-8aa7-4aa0-997d-69eb8c10529d.png)

Ok, let's begin:

## The Script:
The first thing is you should get your own [TMDB API Key here](https://<redacted-host>/reference/intro/authentication#api-key-quick-start). Also, check the directory for your collections. In my case, it was inside `/config/data/data/collections`, instead of @VigibotDev `/var/lib/jellyfin/data/collections`. If you don't get this path right, it wont work.

An additional update is the setting of the media language: I've added two new variables "LANG" and "LOCALE", for both, in my case, the language (pt) and location (pt-BR / Brazil).

File: collections.sh
```
#!/bin/bash

TMDBAPIKEY="{YOUR API KEY HERE}"
DIR="/config/data/data/collections"
TMDBURL="https://<redacted-host>/3/collection"
IMAGEURL="https://<redacted-host>/t/p/original"
LANG="pt"
LOCALE="pt-BR"

for entry in "$DIR"/*; do
    if [ "$entry" == "$DIR/*" ]; then
        continue
    fi

    xmlpath="$entry/collection.xml"
    if [ ! -f "$xmlpath" ]; then
        echo "File not found: \"$xmlpath\""
        continue
    fi
    
    posterpath="$entry/folder.jpg"
    backdroppath="$entry/background.jpg"
    if [ -f "$posterpath" ] && [ -f "$backdroppath" ]; then
        continue
    fi

    tmdb=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "Item/TmdbId" "$xmlpath")

    if [ -z "$tmdb" ]; then
        echo "No TMDb ID in: \"$xmlpath\""
        continue
    fi

    url="$TMDBURL/$tmdb?api_key=$TMDBAPIKEY&append_to_response=images&include_image_language=$LANG,null,en&language=$LOCALE"
    json=$(curl -s "$url")

    if [ -z "$json" ]; then
        echo "Failed to retrieve TMDb data: \"$url\""
        continue
    fi

    if [ ! -f "$posterpath" ]; then
        poster=$(echo "$json" | jq -r .poster_path)

        if [ ! -z "$poster" ] && [ "$poster" != "null" ]; then
            posterurl="$IMAGEURL$poster"
            echo "Downloading poster: \"$posterurl\""
            curl -s "$posterurl" -o "$posterpath"
            echo "Writing poster: \"$posterpath\""
        else
            echo "No poster: \"$entry\""
        fi
    fi

    if [ ! -f "$backdroppath" ]; then
        backdrop=$(echo "$json" | jq -r .backdrop_path)

        if [ ! -z "$backdrop" ] && [ "$backdrop" != "null" ]; then
            backdropurl="$IMAGEURL$backdrop"
            echo "Downloading backdrop: \"$backdropurl\""
            curl -s "$backdropurl" -o "$backdroppath"
            echo "Writing backdrop: \"$backdroppath\""
        else
            echo "No backdrop: \"$entry\""
        fi
    fi
done
```

This is the script we're going to be running. It uses `xmlstarlet` for XML parsing, `curl` for making HTTP requests, and `jq` for JSON parsing, but on my latest install of Jellyfin on Docker, these were all present.

## Accessing the Docker container terminal
In my case, the docker container is called "jellyfin", and that's what I'm using here:
```
sudo docker exec -it jellyfin bash
```

## Creating the script
Once inside, you'll need to navigate to a new folder to store the script, I've created mine in `/data/scripts`:
```bash
mkdir /config/data/scripts
cd /config/data/scripts
```

Once in this folder, we need to create the script file. This docker container is minimal, and don't provide any pre installed editor such as `nano`, `vim` or `vi`, so we'll be creating the file using `echo`. The contents bellow should be placed all together, not one at a time, and is just the same script provided earlier, just in `echo` syntax. Remember to replace `{YOUR API KEY HERE}` with a proper value:
```
echo '#!/bin/bash' > collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo 'DIR="/config/data/data/collections"' >> collections.sh
echo 'TMDBAPIKEY="{YOUR API KEY HERE}"' >> collections.sh
echo 'TMDBURL="https://<redacted-host>/3/collection"' >> collections.sh
echo 'IMAGEURL="https://<redacted-host>/t/p/original"' >> collections.sh
echo 'LANG="pt"' >> collections.sh
echo 'LOCALE="pt-BR"' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo 'for entry in "$DIR"/*; do' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ "$entry" == "$DIR/*" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        continue' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    xmlpath="$entry/collection.xml"' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ ! -f "$xmlpath" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        echo "File not found: \"$xmlpath\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        continue' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    posterpath="$entry/folder.jpg"' >> collections.sh
echo '    backdroppath="$entry/background.jpg"' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ -f "$posterpath" ] && [ -f "$backdroppath" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        continue' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    tmdb=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "Item/TmdbId" "$xmlpath")' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ -z "$tmdb" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        echo "No TMDb ID in: \"$xmlpath\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        continue' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    url="$TMDBURL/$tmdb?api_key=$TMDBAPIKEY&append_to_response=images&include_image_language=$LANG,null,en&language=$LOCALE"' >> collections.sh
echo '    json=$(curl -s "$url")' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ -z "$json" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        echo "Failed to retrieve TMDb data: \"$url\""' >> collections.sh
echo '        continue' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ ! -f "$posterpath" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        poster=$(echo "$json" | jq -r .poster_path)' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '        if [ ! -z "$poster" ] && [ "$poster" != "null" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '            posterurl="$IMAGEURL$poster"' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "Downloading poster: \"$posterurl\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '            curl -s "$posterurl" -o "$posterpath"' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "Writing poster: \"$posterpath\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        else' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "No poster: \"$entry\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        fi' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '    if [ ! -f "$backdroppath" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '        backdrop=$(echo "$json" | jq -r .backdrop_path)' >> collections.sh
echo '' >> collections.sh
echo '        if [ ! -z "$backdrop" ] && [ "$backdrop" != "null" ]; then' >> collections.sh
echo '            backdropurl="$IMAGEURL$backdrop"' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "Downloading backdrop: \"$backdropurl\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '            curl -s "$backdropurl" -o "$backdroppath"' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "Writing backdrop: \"$backdroppath\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        else' >> collections.sh
echo '            echo "No backdrop: \"$entry\"" ' >> collections.sh
echo '        fi' >> collections.sh
echo '    fi' >> collections.sh
echo 'done' >> collections.sh
```

## Running the script
For you to be able to run the script, you need to make it executable:
```
chmod -x collections.sh
```

Once that's done, just run it using:
```
./collections.sh
```

You should get a execution log on the console, looking something like this:
```
root@server:/config/data/scripts# ./collections.sh
Downloading poster: "https://<redacted-host>/t/p/original/8QeWgrqxTVMANlAMNGqXucNLQyf.jpg"
Writing poster: "/config/data/data/collections/A História Sem Fim: Coleção [boxset]/folder.jpg"
Downloading backdrop: "https://<redacted-host>/t/p/original/2IqXJIR1i0f6Ngq3A6rjXhQNqFc.jpg"
Writing backdrop: "/config/data/data/collections/A História Sem Fim: Coleção [boxset]/background.jpg"
... 
```

When the script is finished, you'll be able to use the console again, and that's it, no need to restart the container, nothing, it's already updated, when you load the collection's page on your client, it'll be there.

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
@participant10 

This happened b/c  you selected "Strip Keywords from Title" in the TMDb Box Sets plugin, which made a duplicate entry without the word collection. There are several ways to fix this, I'll outline one method below. 

1. Unselect "Strip Keywords from Title"  option from the TMDb Box Sets in Dashboard->Plugins. 
2. Shutdown the server
3. Delete all collection folders in your Jellyfin data directory \jellyfin\data\collections (you'll see all the collection folders in here)
4. Restart the server
5. In Dashboard->Library go to your Collections and trigger a scan of your library. This will remove all the folders you just deleted.
6. In Dashboard->Scheduled tasks manually run the Scan library for new box sets. This will recreate your collections.
